definitions.text: Spoon or brush pan juices or fat over food while it cooks to keep it moist.
Mix vigorously to make smooth or to incorporate air.
Plunge briefly into boiling salted water, then into ice water to stop the cooking.
Dip in boiling water to loosen the skin.
Mix ingredients until smooth and uniform, by hand or in a blender.
Bake a pastry crust without its filling, lined with paper and weighted with beans or pie weights.
Soak in cold water so it swells before dissolving.
Heat briefly in oil to release their aromas.
Heat a liquid until it bubbles vigorously (100 °C / 212 °F for water).
Brown, then cook slowly, covered, with a small amount of liquid.
Salty solution used to preserve or season food.
Soak meat in salted water to season it and keep it juicy.
Cook under direct, intense heat from above (oven broiler).
Very small, even dice (1–3 mm) of vegetables.
Cut meat, poultry or shrimp almost in half and open it flat so it cooks evenly.
Heat sugar until it melts and turns golden brown.
Cook until their natural sugars brown and develop flavor.
Cut into pieces: roughly chopped pieces are irregular, finely chopped ones small.
Melt gently and remove the milk solids to keep only the clear fat.
Make a stock or broth clear by removing its impurities.
Remove the central part containing the seeds of a fruit (apples, pears...).
Pinch or press pastry edges together to seal and decorate them.
Pour a liquid into a hot pan to dissolve the browned bits stuck to the bottom.
Cut into small, even cubes.
Coat lightly with a dry ingredient such as flour or breadcrumbs.
Pour a liquid in a thin stream over food.
Combine two liquids that don't normally mix (oil and vinegar...) into a smooth, stable mixture.
Brush with a shiny coating (egg, jam, syrup).
Cook with butter, sugar and water until coated with a glossy syrup.
Brush with a sauce during cooking to form a shiny crust.
Vegetables cut into thin matchsticks.
Work a dough by pressing, folding and stretching it until smooth and elastic.
Chop into very small pieces (garlic, herbs, meat).
Diced onion, carrot and celery used as an aromatic base.
Consistency of a sauce thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Boil partially, to finish cooking later by another method.
Remove the thin outer skin with a paring knife or a peeler.
Cook gently in a liquid kept just below a simmer.
Let a yeast dough rise before baking; also test that yeast is active.
Blend or mash food until completely smooth; also the result.
Neat oval shape formed with two spoons (ice cream, mousse, forcemeat).
Boil uncovered to evaporate water and concentrate the flavor.
Lower the heat setting.
Point where beaten eggs and sugar fall from the whisk in a thick ribbon that briefly holds its shape.
Cooked mixture of fat and flour used to thicken sauces.
Cook quickly in a small amount of fat over fairly high heat, tossing or stirring.
Heat to just below boiling.
Plunge briefly into boiling water.
Brown the surface of meat quickly over very high heat.
Add salt, pepper, herbs or spices to enhance the flavor.
Cut or tear into thin strips (cabbage, cheese, cooked meat...).
Pass dry ingredients through a sieve to remove lumps and aerate them.
Cook in a liquid just below the boil, with small bubbles.
Remove fat or foam from the surface of a liquid.
Soak in a hot liquid to extract flavor (tea, spices).
Cook slowly, covered in liquid; also the dish itself.
Cook small pieces quickly over very high heat while stirring constantly, usually in a wok.
Pass through a sieve to separate liquid from solids.
Cook vegetables gently in a little fat until soft, without browning.
Melt, cool, then rewarm chocolate to precise temperatures so it sets glossy and snaps.
Gradually add a hot liquid to eggs to warm them without scrambling.
Make a liquid denser, by reduction or with flour, starch or egg yolks.
Tie poultry or meat with string so it keeps its shape during cooking.
